attempted_axis: Aligned-view re-derivation of the v2 slot-hole park plus the mandated 2026-09-01 parameter-save-area-floor screen, then one declaration-position probe at a position the v2 probes never tested (a 4-byte pad declared FIRST, at the very top of the function's declaration list, rather than at or near the bottom where PROBE2/3/4 all sat).

attributes.decisive_finding: THE v2 PARK'S FRAMING IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT: THIS IS NOT A MISSING RESERVATION, IT IS A MISPLACED ONE. v2 concluded that 'the 4 bytes at 788 must be a compiler temp or inner-block local that retail's source materialised and our reconstruction does not', i.e. that we are short 4 bytes. We are not. slotdiff reports frame 920/920, save set r14/r14 identical, 222 slots on each side, and exactly ONE exclusive slot per side: TARGET-ONLY 796 (3 uses), OURS-ONLY 788 (3 uses). Both builds reserve the SAME 16 bytes in [784..799] and both contain exactly one dead 4-byte word; the dead word simply sits on the opposite side of the two word temps. Reading every (r1) row in the aligned view gives the full decomposition, with the two temps identified by their uses: C = the `keynum` spill (data->keynum, struct offset 0x0C, stored from r0 at 0x3c, ~14 uses) at 784 on BOTH sides; B = the `keydata` parameter home (stored from r28 at 0x48, reloaded at 0x6cc and 0xacc as fn_80010904's first argument); A = a word temp (stored at 0x670, reloaded at 0xa34 and 0xa4c); and an 8-byte 8-aligned FP temp at 800 (`stw r0,800(r1)` / `lfd f0,800(r1)`) IDENTICAL on both sides. TARGET layout: C@784, DEAD@788, B@792, A@796, fp@800 - i.e. the two word temps are packed FLUSH BENEATH the 8-byte FP temp, and the dead word falls between the named local and the temp pair. OURS: C@784, B@788, A@792, DEAD@796, fp@800 - the temps are packed flush ABOVE the named local and the dead word falls under the FP temp. Equivalently: the target's {B,A} pair begins at 792, which is 8-ALIGNED, and ours begins at 788, which is not. This reframing also EXPLAINS v2's PROBE3 exactly, which v2 could not account for: adding 4 bytes at the bottom moved all three of C/B/A up by 4, which is why it closed all six structural words for B and A and simultaneously broke C by pushing it off 784. The correct requirement is therefore NOT 'create a 4-byte temp' but 'move the existing dead word from above A to below B', i.e. shift the {B,A} pair up by 4 while holding C at 784.
attributes.do_not_retry: All of v2's do-not-retry stands (function-scope pad size changes and near-bottom declaration reordering all slide C/B/A as a rigid group). ADDED BY THIS PASS: a dead 4-byte named local declared FIRST, at the very top of the declaration list, is INERT - frame stayed 920 and the slot map was BYTE-IDENTICAL, so it neither reserved a word at 788 nor moved anything. That closes the last untested function-scope declaration POSITION (v2 tested bottom and near-bottom; this tested top), and with it the whole function-scope declaration-position axis, from both ends. Do not spend another probe on where a function-scope local is declared. The live lever is now precisely stated and is an ALIGNMENT question, not a reservation question: make the {keydata-home, word-temp} pair start on an 8-byte boundary (792) instead of 788. Note also that closing this slot alone does NOT make the function exact - 78 of the 85 differing rows are register renaming - so this slot is a prerequisite for webfrank candidacy, not a flip on its own.
attributes.law_screen: claim.law.parameter-save-area-width-sets-the-local-block-floor.20260901.v1 SCREENED EXPLICITLY (the lane's mandated first check) and MEASURED NEGATIVE, with the law's own prescribed diagnostic: the law fires when the frame size AGREES while a slot SET is uniformly displaced, which would mean the floor is wrong. Here the frame agrees but the displacement is NOT uniform - 221 of 222 slots are identical and only the two temps move - so the local block did not move as a unit and the floor is correct. The declared parameter list (f32 frame, AnimData*, f32*, u32*, s32, s32, s32) was audited against this: the only FP parameter is the leading f32 `frame`, an f64/f32 miscount there would shift EVERY memory-resident local by 4, and no such uniform shift exists. Law correctly screened out by its own discriminator. claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order.20260831.v1 APPLIED as the reading frame for the slot decomposition and as the basis for the top-of-list probe. claim.law.local-block-is-bottom-anchored-so-the-lowest-pad-is-the-shift-lever.20260831.v1 SCREENED: consistent with v2's PROBE3 (growing the bottom pad moved the run UP), but it has no lever here because the run must move while its BOTTOM member C stays put - the law moves whole runs, not sub-runs. claim.law.inner-block-pad-reaches-below-the-compiler-temps.20260831.v1 SCREENED, NOT APPLICABLE in the needed direction: it places bytes BELOW the temp group, i.e. below C@784, whereas the 4 bytes must land BETWEEN C and B. claim.law.switch-arm-inner-blocks-overlay-so-hoisting-a-repeated-declaration-does-not-drain-the-low-region.20260831.v1 SCREENED, NOT APPLICABLE: the residual is at the TOP of the local area, immediately under the saved-GPR block (stmw r14,816), not in the low region, and no arm hoisting is involved. claim.law.mwcc-ctr-loop-strength-reduction-is-defeated-by-an-in-body-exit-test.20260831.v1 SCREENED, NOT APPLICABLE: both sides already agree on every loop; the opcode multiset is IDENTICAL (0t) so no mtctr/bdnz asymmetry exists. claim.law.r0-homed-address-temp-forces-the-indexed-store-form.20260901.v1 SCREENED, NOT APPLICABLE: no indexed-store rows; the differing stores are plain stw/lwz with differing displacements. claim.law.dead-nominal-local-area-tracks-declaration-count.20260831.v1 SCREENED and measured NOT to hold for a top-of-list dead 4-byte local in this function (it reserved nothing). claim.law.identical-multiset-is-blind-to-displacements.20260831.v1 carried forward from v2 and re-confirmed (multiset 0t while 85 rows differ).
attributes.measurement_resolution: One 4-byte stack slot, arbitrated on the slotdiff slot map (never on real, per claim.law.real-can-underweight-a-large-alignment-gain). slotdiff headlines frame, save set, and exclusive slots on each side, which is what made the 'same reservation, opposite side' reading visible where v2's per-word regnorm reading was not.
attributes.residual: UNCHANGED and retained at real 172, insns 1047/1047, opcode multiset IDENTICAL (0t), frame 920/920, save set r14 both sides. 85 differing rows in the aligned view: 6 structural (r1)-displacement words from the one misplaced dead slot, ~78 register-renaming words dominated by an f0/f1 cycle across the nine inlined channel loops, and 2 pool-name rows. SEPARATELY NOTED, and deliberately NOT worked: at 0x66c and 0xa70 the target reads named pool symbol lbl_80345838 where ours emits an anonymous pool literal @@794. This is NOT a source defect - the function contains no f64 literal; the constant is MWCC's own int-to-double conversion magic, which the target happens to carry as a named sdata2 symbol - so it is pool-name churn (claim.law.pool-name-churn-is-invisible-to-real-and-fuzzy, claim.law.regnorm-structural-count-was-inflated-by-pool-name-relocs) and not a lever. Recorded here so the next pass does not spend a probe declaring `extern f64 lbl_80345838` inside this function.
